statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is at its floor because the CME equity-index halt leaves no tradable price path; Stress stays elevated on unpriced US-Iran escalation.
recommendation: Path risk is concentrated in the single hour after futures matching resumes at 22:00Z. Outside that window the mapped state remains green with Tail well below the block threshold.
headline: Third hour of the Labor Day halt; crude fades from its high while the 22:00Z restart stays the one mapped danger window
body: CME equity-index futures have been halted since 17:00Z and resume matching at 22:00Z for the Tuesday trade date, while NYSE and Nasdaq stayed shut all day for Labor Day and reopen at 13:30Z tomorrow. NQ's last print is unchanged at 29,565.25, up 40.50 points (+0.14%), inside a narrow 29,530.50-29,682.50 holiday range it had already faded from, so the pre-halt tape showed working retracements and no one-way structure. With no order book there is no price path capable of denying mean reversion, which is why Tail sits at its floor; the same absence is what caps a forward read. The notable change since the previous hour is in energy, which is the channel actually driving risk. WTI October futures settled at 91.48, up only 0.20%, after fading roughly 1.9% from a 93.29 session high into their own 18:30Z close, and Brent is near 96.94, up 0.69% and off an intraday peak close to 97.5. That fade matters: crude retraced from its highs even as fresh escalation headlines landed, which is orderly two-way discovery rather than a one-way impulse. The offsetting development is that Iran's Supreme National Security Council head said on Monday that Tehran plans to declare a maritime exclusion zone running from the line of the US naval blockade toward the Strait of Hormuz, with details expected over days or weeks. That follows the weekend's exchange in which US forces struck three Iranian tankers and Tehran claimed retaliation against US-linked vessels. Because the exclusion zone is announced intent rather than an executed action, it is scored as a slow-burn escalation that lifts Stress, not as the kind of discontinuity that would lift Tail. Cross-assets remain unaligned. European cash closed mixed with the Stoxx 600 just below flat, oil and gas led at +1.29% while healthcare and financials fell, and Asia-Pacific rose overnight. The dollar was the day's other mover, with USD/JPY down about 1% to 154.65, its weakest since February, and gold slipped 0.8% to about 4,390. The latest completed equity session showed unusually wide internal dispersion, semiconductors broadly higher against sharp declines in several megacaps, which is a Stress and Confidence input rather than a Tail amplifier. US Treasury cash markets were closed today; the most recent H.15 values, for 3 September, are 4.34% at two years and 4.77% at ten. VIX last traded near 15.3, historically calm. The single concentrated risk is the 22:00Z restart, where roughly five hours of unpriced escalation would meet the thinnest liquidity of the week. That hour alone is mapped to WATCH; path risk then decays through Asia and rises again modestly into the 13:30Z cash reopen. All post-halt structure is described conditionally because none of it is observable at the assessment cutoff.

lookbackSummary: Twenty-three of the last twenty-four hourly Claude assessments are available; the 2026-09-06T21:00Z slot has no published assessment and is marked unavailable. The window was uniformly green with EA_ON throughout and Tail confined to a 5-10% band. Stress ran at 54-60% overnight, rose to 61-64% through the US afternoon as crude extended and holiday liquidity thinned, and eased to 62% into the halt. Confidence fell from 86% to 75% across the stretch as live price evidence disappeared with the 17:00Z halt. Dominant mode was normal apart from the 14:00Z, 16:00Z and 17:00Z slots, which were mixed while the energy-versus-equity divergence widened.
outlookSummary: The next twenty-four hours are governed by market structure rather than macro. Futures stay halted for three more hours, so the opening forecast slots carry no tradable path and Tail sits at its floor. The one elevated slot is the 22:00Z restart, where several hours of unpriced US-Iran escalation, including Iran's announced intent to declare a Hormuz-area exclusion zone, would meet the thinnest liquidity of the window; that hour alone maps to WATCH. Path risk then decays through the Asian and European sessions as depth rebuilds, with a secondary rise into the 13:30Z US cash reopen, the first regular session after the three-day weekend and the first full-depth pricing of the weekend's tanker exchange. All post-halt structure is framed conditionally because none of it is observable at the assessment cutoff; only the pre-halt range, its fade, and crude's retracement from its session high into the 18:30Z energy close are stated as fact. NFIB at 10:00Z and the weekly ADP print at 12:15Z are the only scheduled US releases inside the window, with PPI and claims on Thursday and CPI on Friday as the week's principal checkpoints.
